expectations.text: TokenBucket class comment in the .h says what the class is for and states its thread-safety guarantee explicitly
expectations.evidence: Class comment explains the token-bucket model and has an explicit paragraph: "Thread safety: fully thread-safe. Any number of threads may call Acquire and TryAcquire concurrently on the same instance." plus fairness and lifetime caveats.

expectations.text: Every public method declaration in the .h has a contract comment: what it does, parameter meaning/units, return value semantics
expectations.evidence: Ctor, Acquire, TryAcquire, capacity(), refill_rate(), and even the deleted copy ops all carry contract comments, e.g. "Constructs a bucket that holds at most `capacity` tokens and refills at `refill_rate` tokens per second."

expectations.text: Acquire documents its blocking semantics (and timeout behavior if a timeout is offered); TryAcquire documents True/False semantics and that nothing is consumed on failure
expectations.evidence: Acquire: "Blocks the calling thread until `n` tokens are available... Never fails and never times out." TryAcquire: "Returns true and consumes exactly `n` tokens if at least that many are currently available; otherwise returns false and consumes nothing."

expectations.text: Units are documented for rates and durations (tokens per second, seconds)
expectations.evidence: "refills at `refill_rate` tokens per second" (ctor), "// Refill rate in tokens per second; > 0." (member), "the long-run admission rate never exceeds `refill_rate` tokens per second" (class comment).

expectations.text: Function comments are third-person declarative with proper punctuation
expectations.evidence: All function comments use third-person verbs with terminal periods: "Constructs a bucket...", "Blocks the calling thread...", "Attempts to consume...", "Returns the bucket's maximum token count...", "Adds tokens accrued..."

expectations.text: The .cc does not duplicate the .h contract comments; its comments explain implementation choices (e.g. why sleeping outside the lock / condition-variable usage)
expectations.evidence: .cc comments are implementation-focused: file comment describes the lazy-refill strategy, RefillLocked explains the clock guard and why last_refill_ advances when capped, and Acquire explains deadline-based cv_.wait_for ("tokens accrue from the passage of time alone, so no other thread will necessarily signal us") and the one-tick minimum wait.

expectations.text: No comments that restate the code; no Author: lines; // style used consistently
expectations.evidence: No Author: lines (license boilerplate only); // style used throughout including the file headers; comments explain rationale (e.g. why available_ is a double) rather than restating statements.

expectations.text: If any call site passes a bare literal argument, it uses the /*param_name=*/value comment form (vacuously true if no such call exists)
expectations.evidence: The usage example annotates ambiguous literals: "TokenBucket bucket(/*capacity=*/10, /*refill_rate=*/100.0);". Remaining literals (example's Acquire(1), which has a trailing explanatory comment; Clock::duration(1)) are single-argument calls whose meaning is evident, not ambiguous bare-literal sites.

summary.notes: Full-detail CC2 output with exhaustive header contracts (thread safety, fairness, lifetime, preconditions), units throughout, and .cc comments confined to implementation rationale.
